core_obligations: Reduce to charts: choose a scheme $U$ surjective \'etale over $T$ and schemes $U_i$ surjective \'etale over $T_i \times_T U$; $\{U_i \to U\}$ is an fpqc covering (cited Topologies on Spaces lemmas), so the scheme-side proposition applies to it (proof lines 838-850).

Transport data: a compatible family $b_i : T_i \to B$ composes with $U_i \to T_i$ to give $a_i : U_i \to B$; the scheme case yields a unique $a : U \to B$ with $a_i$ the composition of $a$ with $U_i \to U$ (proof lines 850-857).

Conclude: uniqueness forces $a \circ \mathrm{pr}_0 = a \circ \mathrm{pr}_1$ on $U \times_T U$; since $T = U/(U \times_T U)$ as a sheaf, $a$ comes from a unique $b : T \to B$, and the diagram chase identifies $b$ as the equalizer element (proof lines 857-864).
proof_roadmap: Take the scheme-side fpqc sheaf property as the key input.
Move to surjective \'etale charts over $T$ and the covering members.
Get the chart-level morphism from the scheme case and descend it through the sheaf quotient.
difficulty_reason: The proof takes the scheme-side fpqc sheaf proposition as the key fact, then runs an explicit \'etale-chart reduction: lift a compatible family $b_i : T_i \to B$ through charts $U_i \to T_i \times_T U$, obtain $a : U \to B$ from the scheme case, use uniqueness to get $a \circ \mathrm{pr}_0 = a \circ \mathrm{pr}_1$ on $U \times_T U$, and conclude with the sheaf-quotient presentation $T = U/(U \times_T U)$ plus the final diagram bookkeeping.
